cells.tense: You are here, and the hands have gotten quiet around what matters.
cells.act: use the finished thing for an hour instead of improving it
cells.ask: Take something whose finish has held for a while and use it, not improve it, with no clock running.
cells.core:
The hands have gotten quiet around what matters. Small choices that used to take a debate now take a glance. You don't chase certainty and you don't get hooked by the bright new lead; you read what's there and keep your attention on it. The weight of that is light because nothing in you is arguing with it.

What is making the rounds in you is probably not all your own invention. It arrives through you from work already done, and it isn't less yours for that. Spend an hour with something finished, using it rather than improving it, so what it's for stays as full as what it could be. Leaving it alone is the whole exercise.

cells.tense: You will need the answer to matter before it has had time to arrive.
cells.act: bring the two sides of your thinking into one plan
cells.ask: Set beside each other what pulls at you and the turn you want to make, and leave the two of them there.
cells.core:
A decision is coming and you are already holding rehearsal — the meeting, the way it might go — and the heavier it gets, the more you reach for the next thing before this one has shown its face. The forward lean is real, and it's running faster than the moment it belongs to.

Stop drafting and gather what is already there. Neither the turn you want to make nor the pull on you is the enemy; both belong together. Set beside each other what matters this week and the way you'd like the week to go, and leave the two of them side by side without rearranging anything. The stillness underneath can be slept in once the pieces sit together.

cells.tense: The hand that used to go straight to the good thing folded, at some point, and stayed folded.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Count what a closing left you — the gains, not what it took — and keep the tally somewhere you'll pass it.
cells.core:
The hand that once went straight to the good thing folded, and stayed folded. What matters gets measured by what it might take instead of what it holds. Things finished long back get taken out and turned over, and you reach for the same familiar tasks because they can't fail. There's a steadiness in that, and also a quiet — the willingness that used to come naturally has its shoulders down.

Wanting was not the problem. Walk back through one change that landed and count what it left behind — gains only, tallied somewhere you'll pass it. Nobody is asking you to reach for more; the meeting is with what is already sitting there, and the count can be small.

cells.tense: Nowhere have you said what you're building, though the building has been going on.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Give the build one plain sentence about where it's going, then put in today's part of it.
cells.core:
The story heads somewhere you have not claimed. You tell people you're tidying up, keeping it simple — while the thing you're actually tending has been built past that, board by board. When it's working, you can give the build its plain name and keep going in the same breath, no speech attached, no shrug either.

So give it one plain sentence — to somebody, or to yourself in the mirror — about where the whole thing is heading, then do today's part of it. No revelation, no self-deprecating bow. What you have already been doing is the evidence, and the sentence just stands next to it.
